newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Canadian Mountie initiates Busang gold inquiries.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Mountie initiates Busang gold inquiries.

text.p: A Royal Canadian Mounted Police officer held talks with Indonesian police on Friday as part of preliminary investigations into the Busang gold scandal, officials said.

Brigadier-General Ahwil Luthan, secretary of Indonesia's National Central Bureau which handles investigations requiring Interpol assistance, said he held talks with Singapore-based Mountie liaison officer for Southeast Asia, Douglas Herda.
"We had a meeting today to discuss many things, including Busang," Luthan told Reuters. "We exchanged information on Busang."

Herda declined to give details of his visit to Jakarta except to say it was linked to Busang, a once-fabled gold discovery in Borneo island that was comprehensively debunked last weekend amid allegations of falsified data.
"Any information will have to come from Canada," he said, declining to say if he would meet government officials and former partners in the collapsed Busang project.
Canadian diplomat Rene Cremonese said Herda was scheduled to meet Indonesian police but had no details. "He (Herda) is here for preliminary discussions on the issue of Bre-X."

Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd was delisted from the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday after its Busang property, once touted as the richest gold find this century, was proven a sham.
An independent audit of Busang in East Kalimantan province by consultant Strathcona Minerals Services Ltd of Canada showed there was no economic gold deposit there.
Strathcona said data on the Busang property had been falsified on a scale "without precedent in mining history".
Bre-X on Thursday won court protection from creditors, similar to bankruptcy protection in the United States.
In a letter to the Canadian police, Bre-X chief executive David Walsh alleged a fraud had been perpetrated against his company, but he did not identify a suspect.

A second fraud complaint was filed by the Ontario Securities Commission, Canada's top securities regulator, which is conducting its own investigation of Bre-X for possible violations of insider trading and disclosure laws.
